cases.prompt: We support an internal ledger service in three applications. One of them has no ledger dependency at all and must still start. Should I write an auto-configuration, add a starter, or just declare the client bean?
expectations: Chooses starter plus auto-configuration because more than one application consumes the integration
Guards the bean with ConditionalOnClass so the application without the dependency still starts
Guards the bean with ConditionalOnMissingBean so an application can override the default client

cases.prompt: Our auto-configured Stripe client is created even though the application declares its own StripeClient bean, and both end up in the context.
expectations: Identifies that ConditionalOnMissingBean is evaluated against definitions registered so far
Requires registration in the AutoConfiguration.imports file and an explicit after or before relation
Adds a context runner test for the back-off case and the create case

cases.prompt: acme.ledger.url is correct in application-prod.yaml but the app still uses the value from application.yaml. The jar runs with -Dspring.profiles.active=prod.
expectations: Checks the property source order and confirms a profile file beats its non-profile twin
Verifies the file is actually loaded, for example with the actuator env or configprops endpoint
Checks that -D system properties outrank config data files

cases.prompt: Bind acme.ledger into a typed record with a URL, a connect timeout, a retry block, and a currency list, and make the app refuse to start when a value is missing.
expectations: Uses a record with ConfigurationProperties and Validated rather than Value injections
Applies NotBlank or NotNull plus Positive constraints and a nested Valid record
Uses DefaultValue for optional keys and reports the startup failure as intended fail-fast behavior

cases.prompt: Should we set spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true on our Spring Boot 3.5 service? Controllers block on JDBC and we are on Java 21.
expectations: States it is an option with tradeoffs, not a default, and requires a load test before and after
Notes that thread pool properties stop applying and that the datasource pool and semaphores become the real bound
Warns about pinned carrier threads when blocking inside synchronized and about daemon threads needing spring.main.keep-alive

cases.prompt: Add component scanning over our third-party SDK package so their client gets wired automatically. What is wrong with that?
expectations: Rejects component scanning of a third-party package because it forces the dependency into the build
Proposes the starter or an explicit auto-configuration with ConditionalOnClass instead
Requires an application-owned client bean when the integration is single-application
